before: Cost Synergies (Hard Synergies): Eliminate duplicate corporate overhead (SG&A, HR, Legal, IT), consolidate manufacturing facilities, realize bulk procurement discounts, optimize supply chain logistics.
Revenue Synergies (Soft Synergies): Cross-sell complementary products to existing customer bases, expand target products into acquirer's international distribution channels, bundle solutions.
Financial & Tax Synergies: Lower cost of capital through larger borrowing capacity, utilization of accumulated Net Operating Losses (NOLs), tax inversion/optimization.

Net Value Creation: Compare Net Present Value of Synergies against Acquisition Premium paid to target shareholders.

after: Pillar 1 — Market Attractiveness: Size, growth rate, customer segments, profitability, and macro regulatory tailwinds.

Pillar 3 — Company Capabilities & Synergies (efficiencies gained by combining businesses), core competencies, brand transferable equity, distribution leverage, operational fit.
